title: The Fall of Constantinople
description: April-May 1453. The player commands the last defenders of Byzantium under Constantine XI. Hold the Theodosian Walls against Mehmed II's siege: repair breaches from bombard fire, guard the sea walls along the Golden Horn, and survive repeated assaults. Defeat comes if the Hagia Sophia district falls; victory means holding until the final assault is broken.

issues_found: Player 2 (Turks) fields no Janissaries, the engine's Turkish unique unit and the iconic core of Mehmed II's assault troops; instead the Ottoman host is built from Knights, Cavaliers and Crossbowmen, a generic European composition. This substitution was avoidable.

Mehmed II is represented by a CAVALIER and Giustiniani by a CHAMPION renamed via triggers — acceptable given no engine heroes exist, but the Ottoman commander as a mailed Frankish-style Cavalier reads as a Latin knight rather than a Sultan.
No third player for the Genoese/Venetian contingent, even though the narration turns on Giustiniani's Genoese wavering after his fall; his soldiers are indistinguishable from Byzantine line troops.
TREE_PALM_FOREST x10 is botanically wrong for the Bosphorus in spring 1453 and an avoidable choice given the engine's oak/pine sets.

The Golden Horn strand is narrated (ships dragged overland, sea walls to be guarded) but implemented purely as land-unit spawns: no docks, warships, transports or any naval object appears anywhere in the roster, so the outflanking of the sea walls is asserted rather than shown.
Only 2 gates and 78 stone wall segments stand in for the triple Theodosian line; there is no outer wall/moat layering, so the 'repair the breach' mechanic plays out on a single curtain.
The victory narration ('Constantinople stands, and the Empire endures') asserts a counterfactual outcome for the historical event the scenario names.
